newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egypt says biotech ban excludes wheat, seeks shpt.
newsitem.headline: Egypt says biotech ban excludes wheat, seeks shpt.

text.p: Egypt's main grains buyer said on Monday he was informed by officials at the health ministry that wheat imports were excluded "for the time being" from a decree requiring proof that grain imports have not been genetically altered.
He also said he was seeking 50,000 tonnes of wheat.
Samir el-Shakankiri told Reuters he had been informed of the decision a few hours ago and that he wanted to buy 50,000 tonnes of U.S. or French wheat for delivery in August as soon as possible.
The deadline for bids is 0730 GMT on July 22 and Shakankiri said he had the right to cancel the tender at any time.
"I was told to take any action I chose with regards to buying wheat," he added. Shakankiri had told Reuters earlier he would not enter the market for up to one month because of the decree.

Traders and agriculture officials say there is no genetically-engineered wheat on the market. The decree, which was made available late last week, has upset traders but was not expected to harm Egypt's wheat imports.
Traders were unavailable to comment on the amended decree.
